title: Paired-survey batches: every training step sees the same places in all three photographs, not one photograph at a time
hypothesis: The baseline (experiment 1) did not learn three photographs — it learned one. Its train_capture_diagnostics read 0.015 on truedop_2023 (99% usable) but 1.401 on truedop_2022 and 1.533 on bb_dop20, i.e. the two other TRAINING photographs score almost as badly as the held-out one (1.651). The cause is in model/train.py: each epoch runs `for img in imgs:` with a complete 72,712-position lattice pass per photograph, so the model fits bb_dop20, then overwrites it with truedop_2022, then overwrites that with truedop_2023 — within-epoch catastrophic forgetting, with the cosine schedule ending on the 2023 pass. The shared trunk never receives a gradient that says 'these three different-looking crops are the SAME place' at the same time; it only ever receives 'this crop is cell k' from one survey at a time, which is exactly the single-photograph pixel-fingerprint regime the era was opened to escape. The limiting factor on the 2024 score is therefore not yet any invariance mechanism — it is that the three-survey training signal the era provides is not actually being applied. Building every batch from the same lattice positions extracted from all three photographs (same heading, same cell label) applies that signal directly: within one optimizer step the trunk is pushed to produce one cell-belief from three exposures of one place, which penalises features that only hold in one survey and rewards the structure (roads, building footprints, block layout) that all three share. Whether 3 MB of weights is still enough to store three separate fingerprints per cell instead is the open question this experiment makes measurable for the first time — the current baseline cannot answer it because it never tried to hold three.
method: ONE change, in model/train.py only: replace the sequential per-photograph loop with paired-position interleaving. Each chunk draws a set of lattice positions, extracts the crop at each position from EVERY training capture with one shared random heading per position, and the resulting union (positions x captures) is shuffled into mini-batches, so no mini-batch is single-survey and the epoch no longer ends on one photograph. An epoch is still one full pass over the lattice x all three captures (218,136 views, identical compute to the baseline); the loss, targets, model, decode and export are untouched. Per-capture train top-1 is added to the epoch log line and train_info.json so the record shows whether all three surveys are being learned jointly.
expected_outcome: Firm prediction (this is what the change mechanically guarantees if the model has the capacity): the three train_capture_diagnostics converge — bb_dop20 and truedop_2022 drop from 1.53 / 1.40 to below 0.3, and truedop_2023 rises from 0.015 to at most ~0.2 as it now shares weights instead of owning them. Primary (held-out truedop_2024): improves from 1.651; predicted range 0.9–1.3, with the gain coming mostly from false-fix rate falling (68% -> below 45%) as the cell beliefs stop keying on one survey's exact intensities, and usable rising from 3% to 15–35%. If instead the training diagnostics converge but 2024 stays >= 1.5, the model has stored three independent fingerprints per cell and the next experiment must restrict capacity or add an explicit cross-survey consistency term — a clean, informative negative. If the training diagnostics do NOT converge, the implementation is wrong (check the per-capture top-1 log line).
eli5: We handed the model three different aerial photographs of Berlin so it would learn the city rather than one picture of it — but the training routine showed it the whole first photo, then the whole second, then the whole third, like cramming three textbooks one after another the night before an exam. By the time it finished the third it had forgotten the first two, and the test (a fourth photo it has never seen) went badly. This experiment shuffles the three photos together so that every single study session shows the same street corners in all three photographs side by side. That forces it to notice what stays the same between the photos — the roads, the building shapes — instead of memorising the exact colours of one of them.

stages.name: Camera frame
stages.detail: 128×128 px daytime crop, Berlin only; trained on three survey photographs, scored on a fourth it never saw

stages.name: Feature extractor
stages.detail: small strided conv stack that turns the frame into a compact texture fingerprint (last layer 160 channels)

stages.name: Map-cell classifier
stages.detail: scores all ~3,000 128 m map tiles of Berlin and picks the tile this view belongs to — localization as multiple choice, not coordinate guessing

stages.name: Local belief pooling
stages.detail: gathers the belief spread over the winning tile AND its 8 neighbours, and places the fix at the balance point of that local cluster instead of snapping to one tile's centre

stages.name: Within-cell offset
stages.detail: small head that nudges the fix from the pooled balance point to the exact spot

stages.name: Confidence gate
stages.detail: confidence = the belief mass on the winning tile plus its 8 neighbours — a vote split across adjacent tiles still counts as knowing where you are; belief scattered across distant tiles still reads as unsure and the drone abstains

stages.name: Training signal
stages.detail: NEW: each study batch shows the same map positions in all three survey photographs at once (same heading, same tile label), instead of one whole photograph after another — the baseline's photo-by-photo passes made it forget two of the three surveys every epoch. Labels, loss, schedule and total views per epoch are unchanged.

implementation_brief:
Edit ONLY model/train.py. model/model.py is NOT touched (CellLocNet, loss_fn, export_onnx, grid_dims, CELL_PX all stay exactly as they are).

1. load_scene(): unchanged — it already returns `imgs` as the list of ALL train-bucket images in `buckets(meta, 'train')` order and `crops` as the full train lattice. Keep the data contract: only `buckets(meta, 'train')` images are opened; the eval capture (buckets(meta, 'eval'), truedop_2024) must never be opened in any form.

2. Replace extract_chunk(meta, img, crops, indices, rng) with a paired version `extract_chunk(meta, imgs, crops, indices, rng)` that takes the LIST of capture images. For each lattice index i in `indices`: draw ONE heading `angle = rng.uniform(0, 360)`, then for every capture image k in imgs append `extract_crop(imgs[k], cx, cy, angle)` to xs, the containing-cell index to cells, (cx, cy) to pos, and k to caps. Return (x_uint8 [N*K,3,128,128], cell_idx [N*K] int64, pos [N*K,2] float32, cap_idx [N*K] int64). The order within the chunk does not matter because the mini-batch permutation below shuffles it; the point is that the chunk contains every drawn position in every capture.

3. train_area(): restructure the epoch loop so there is NO `for img in imgs:` outer pass. Per epoch: `order = rng.permutation(len(crops))`; iterate `for start in range(0, len(order), POS_PER_CHUNK)` where POS_PER_CHUNK = max(1, CHUNK_SIZE // len(imgs)) (so a chunk still holds ~CHUNK_SIZE = 4096 crops total and memory stays bounded — with three captures that is 1365 positions × 3 = 4095 crops). Call the new extract_chunk with `imgs`, then build mini-batches of BATCH_SIZE=64 from `torch.randperm(n)` over the whole chunk exactly as now (so each mini-batch mixes positions AND captures; with 1365 positions × 3 captures in a chunk, a batch of 64 holds ~64 distinct (position,capture) draws, and every position's three exposures are trained within the same chunk). Loss computation per batch is byte-for-byte what it is now: `logits, off_pred = model.training_outputs(xb)`; `soft_t = make_soft_targets(pb, ...)`; `off_t = residual_offset_target(model, logits, pb, meta)`; `loss = loss_fn(logits, off_pred, soft_t, off_t)`; Adam lr 1e-3, CosineAnnealingLR(T_max=epochs, eta_min=1e-4) stepped once per epoch — all unchanged. Views per epoch must still equal len(crops) * len(imgs) (218,136 for Berlin) so compute matches experiment 1.

4. Logging: in addition to the existing epoch line (loss, top1, mean_max_softmax, views, lr), accumulate per-capture top-1 (correct/seen split by cap_idx) and print it as e.g. `top1_by_capture={'bb_dop20': 0.71, 'truedop_2022': 0.70, 'truedop_2023': 0.72}` using the bucket names from load_scene (return `names` from load_scene, or recompute `list(buckets(meta,'train'))`). Add to the returned train_info dict: `"capture_sampling": "paired-position interleave, shared heading per position"`, `"captures": names`, `"positions_per_chunk": POS_PER_CHUNK`, and `"final_train_top1_by_capture": {name: value}`. Keep every existing train_info key (`n_train_crops`, `distinct_vantages_seen`, `full_lattice_epochs`, `final_train_top1`, `chunk_size`, `max_crops_per_bucket_arg`, `init`: 'from-scratch', etc.).

5. Update the module docstring to describe the paired-survey interleave and why (the sequential per-photograph pass forgot two of three captures each epoch).

Contracts to preserve (frozen scorer depends on them): train.py CLI `--area --out-dir --data-dir --epochs --max-crops-per-bucket --seed` unchanged (`--max-crops-per-bucket` still accepted and only logged); export remains `<out>/models/<area>.onnx` via export_onnx taking 1x3x128x128 float32 in [0,1] and returning [[u, v, conf]] with u,v normalized map coords and conf in [0,1] — untouched because model.py is untouched; exported ONNX stays 3.08 MB (<= 4 MiB) and host latency ~2 ms (<= 250 ms). Python 3.11 syntax only. Syntax-check with `.venv/bin/python -c "import model.train, model.model"`.

Do NOT add a consistency/contrastive loss, do NOT change augmentation beyond the shared heading per position, do NOT change epochs, LR, batch size, chunk memory budget, or anything in model/model.py — this experiment isolates the batch composition change alone.
